title: Teriyaki Chicken Bowl
subtitle: Sticky glazed chicken thighs over rice with steamed broccoli
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs are marinated in a soy, mirin, honey, and sake glaze, then pan-fried until the sauce caramelises into a sticky coating. Served over basmati rice with steamed broccoli and spring onions. A quick dinner that comes together in 30 minutes once the marinade time is done.
sourceNotes: Based on the Japanese teriyaki technique. The glaze is a simple ratio of soy, mirin, sake, and honey that can be applied to fish or tofu as well as chicken.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the chicken up to 24 hours ahead in the fridge. This deepens the flavour significantly.

content.text: The cornflour mixed into the marinade helps the glaze cling to the chicken and thicken quickly in the pan. Without it, the sauce runs off and does not caramelise properly.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, honey, sake, and cornflour together in a bowl until the cornflour dissolves.
Add the chicken thighs to the marinade. Turn to coat. Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the rice according to packet instructions or in a rice cooker.
Remove the chicken from the marinade. Reserve the marinade.
Heat a dry frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken thighs skin-side down. Cook for 6 minutes until golden.
Flip the chicken. Cook for 4 more minutes.
Pour in the reserved marinade. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, turning the chicken to coat, until the sauce is thick and sticky.
Steam the broccoli for 4 minutes until bright green and just tender.
Slice the chicken. Serve over rice with broccoli and spring onions. Drizzle with sesame oil.

items.symptom: Glaze is burning in the pan
items.cause: Honey caramelises fast at high heat
items.fix: Reduce heat to medium when adding marinade.

items.cause: Too much liquid or cornflour not mixed in well
items.fix: Cook on high heat and stir constantly for 2 minutes.
Pull chicken when internal temperature reaches 74C.
